stem: A machine is stopped and its display is dark, but clearing the fault would require removing a guard near a spring-loaded mechanism. The operator procedure does not assign that action to Technician I. What should the technician conclude?
choices: The dark display proves all hazardous energy is gone, so guard removal is routine operator care
The visible spring and guard boundary are warning signs that the task may involve stored energy or servicing, so the technician should stop at the operator boundary and refer the work
The task is safe if a second worker watches the controls
The technician may proceed because mechanical energy is not covered by hazardous-energy controls
rationale: A stopped or dark machine does not prove that all hazardous energy is controlled. Guard removal and stored mechanical energy are signals that the task may cross into servicing or energy-control work outside the Technician I operator procedure.
